issue.title: Right-size the scheduled contention soak so it can gate again
issue.description: The scheduled contention-test job has never fit the hosted 2-CPU runner: it runs the full suite three times with 26 workers pinned to two CPUs, collection alone is about 31 minutes, and the runner is shut down around 37 minutes. This unblock marks it observed-only with continue-on-error, but the lane needs a deliberately smaller subset or runner shape before it can gate again, or it should be removed intentionally.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: This is a structural CI capacity failure, not a flake: contention-test has never passed since the scheduled Full CI lane was created on 2026-08-27. With SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=3, 26 workers, and taskset pinned to two CPUs, the job cannot fit the 90-minute hosted-runner budget; observed runs receive shutdown around 37 minutes, and the estimated full runtime is roughly 2.7 hours.

payload.entry: Backlog triage 2026-10-26: sase-1lt was closed as a duplicate of this bead. Its fresher evidence: in .github/workflows/telemetry.yml the contention-test job (SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=1, 26 workers, dist=worksteal) still ends with 'The runner has received a shutdown signal' about 22-31 min in on every run (e.g. 40332111568 on 2026-10-26, 40213624649, 38936218963), well under its 90-min timeout-minutes; the likely cause is the hosted runner being killed for resources under 26 xdist workers (unproven).
